Can the bank use my digital records or electronic signatures as legal evidence against me in court?

Yes, electronic records, including those with electronic signatures that meet the Bank's requirements and applicable laws, are considered valid, accurate, and authentic. They have the same legal effect as signed hard-copy documents and can be used as evidence in court proceedings to prove their contents. (cimb_personal_loan.pdf, p.11)

Is the bank responsible if I experience delays in accessing my loan funds due to their fraud or anti-money laundering security checks?

No, the bank is not liable for any delays that occur in connection with security processes performed for fraud detection, anti-money laundering, anti-financing-terrorism purposes, or to comply with any sanctions, laws, or regulations. (cimb_personal_loan.pdf, p.5)

What actions can the bank take if my loan-to-value or sell-down ratios are exceeded?

If the ratios are exceeded, the bank may, at its sole discretion and upon reasonable notice, require you to reduce your liabilities, cancel or reduce your facility, withhold further drawings, demand additional collateral, or enforce the existing collateral (standard_chartered_loan.pdf, p.6).

Yes, electronic records and instructions are considered final and conclusive evidence of the information and your agreements, provided there is no manifest or clerical error on the bank's part. (cimb_personal_loan.pdf, p.11)

How is the interest on my CIBC personal loan calculated and applied to my balance?

Interest is calculated daily by multiplying your outstanding principal balance by the daily interest factor based on the current interest rate. The daily charges are then added together for the statement period to determine the total monthly interest. This interest is compounded monthly, meaning unpaid interest from the previous month is added to your loan balance, and the bank may charge interest on that interest. (cibc_personal_loan.pdf, p.5)

What happens if I move out of Canada while I have an active personal loan with CIBC?

If you are no longer a resident of Canada, CIBC may end your loan agreement without your permission. Additionally, you must immediately pay all amounts owing under the loan, regardless of whether they are currently due, and you are responsible for paying any applicable withholding taxes. (cibc_personal_loan.pdf, p.8)

What circumstances might lead to a default or potential termination of my loan agreement?

The loan agreement may be impacted if you fail to pay other debts when due, if you pass away or become mentally unsound, if you enter into bankruptcy or insolvency proceedings, if you leave Singapore permanently, or if any legal proceedings (civil or criminal) are initiated against you. Can CIBC take money from my other bank accounts to cover costs related to my personal loan agreement?

Yes. If you owe money under this indemnity clause and do not have a credit balance on your loan, CIBC may take funds from any of your other accounts with them or their affiliates—including joint accounts—to satisfy the claim, though they cannot take money from your registered retirement savings plan (RRSP) or registered retirement income fund (RRIF). (cibc_personal_loan.pdf, p.10)

How is the interest on my loan calculated?

Interest is calculated using the formula: sum of (Actual balance of the Loan x No. of days that the actual balance is maintained x Interest rate) divided by 365. The actual balance includes the day-end balance of the principal, overdue principal, and actual overdue interest, while the number of days refers to the period during which that balance remains unchanged (standard_chartered_loan.pdf, p.3).
